description: The Global Agro-Ecological Zones programme of FAO and IIASA applies the Agro-Ecological Zones modelling framework, developed over several decades, to assess natural resources for agriculture. It uses land evaluation principles and the eco-physiological, climatic and soil requirements of crops to evaluate suitability and production potential of individual crops under given input and management levels, and identifies resource limits, production risks, irrigation water demand and adaptation options under current and future climate. Version 5 is now available on a new FAO data site, while the GAEZ v4 portal remains online with a map viewer and data feeds in RSS and DCAT formats and a search API. Coverage is global and gridded. Access is free; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: results are model estimates that depend on climate scenarios and input assumptions. For simulation it provides crop suitability, attainable yields and water demand under climate scenarios for agricultural hazard exposure, drought and adaptation planning. Related catalogue records include EarthStat, GLOBIOM and FAOSTAT.
